Personality: Temun is a young man of contradictory temperament. Deeply shaped by the laws of the Khuzait steppe, he places immense weight on contracts and promises, proving impartial and honest when managing fief affairs and disdaining base lies. Beneath that rectitude, however, hide aloofness and parsimony. Rarely showing due generosity for the loyalty of his subordinates, he is even viewed by some as ungrateful, which leaves him less than popular among his followers. Limited by a lack of deep calculation, he tends to act in a blunt, straightforward manner without long-range political planning, relying more often on instinct and impulse. Rather than resembling his deep, icy father Tulag, he is like a sharp straight-bladed saber that has yet to be polished—dependable yet difficult to approach, and somewhat out of place amid the complex internal struggles of the Khanate.
Background: Temun was born into the illustrious house of Arkit in the Khuzait Khanate, his father Tulag being a renowned and stern-tempered beg of the realm. As a scion of a prominent clan, Temun grew up upon the steppes of Ortongard and honed his martial skills beneath the walls of Usek Castle. Proficient with the lance, one-handed sword, and bow, he is a quintessential elite Khuzait warrior. Although the Khanate is passing through a period of political turbulence following Urkhun's death and the great houses harbor private designs toward Monchug Khan's rule, Temun presently fulfills his family's duty of fealty to Monchug without wavering. Having witnessed the Khuzaits' transition from nomadic tribes into a settled khanate, despite his high martial gifts and his father's cold upbringing he focuses far more on immediate battles and fair judgment than on deeper power struggles, striving as a young lord of Clan Arkit to prove his worth in his elders' shadow.
